summary: This memo gives the BGP working group recommendation on how to advertise a default route in versions 2 and 3 of the Border Gateway Protocol. A default route is the catch-all path used when no more specific route exists. It is historic.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 1397 explains how a BGP2 or BGP3 speaker can advertise a default route to a peer. The peer can use the named border gateway for destinations not listed in its routing table.

questions: how to advertise a default route in bgp
how do bgp2 and bgp3 advertise a default route
subtitle: A recommendation for advertising default routes in BGP versions 2 and 3.

tldr.problem: A BGP peer with an incomplete routing table needs to learn which border gateway can handle destinations not listed in that table.
tldr.mechanism: The recommendation advertises network 0.0.0.0 in an UPDATE message and uses NEXT_HOP to identify the default gateway.
tldr.outcome: The RFC applies to BGP2 and BGP3 and is Historic; it notes that default-route advertisement is built into BGP4.

today: RFC 1397 is Historic. It applies to BGP2 and BGP3 and notes that default-route advertisement is built into BGP4.

sections.title: Purpose of a Default Route
sections.content:
A default route gives a BGP peer a next hop for destinations that are not listed explicitly in its routing table. The memo says this can help routers that cannot maintain a complete routing table and can reduce the need to configure static defaults.

If more than one default gateway is advertised, a speaker can express a preference for one entry point over another.
sections.plainLanguage: A default route provides a fallback gateway when a router has no more specific route. A peer can also receive a preference among advertised default gateways.

sections.title: Advertising the Default
sections.content:
A default route is carried in an UPDATE message with the Network field set to 0.0.0.0. The NEXT_HOP attribute gives the address of a border gateway for destinations absent from the peer's routing table.

The memo says the ORIGIN attribute should be 2 (INCOMPLETE), the AS_PATH follows conventional advertisement rules, and INTER-AS-METRIC may express preferences among multiple defaults. UNREACHABLE indicates that a previously advertised default has become unreachable.
sections.plainLanguage: The UPDATE identifies 0.0.0.0 as the default route and names a border gateway as its next hop. Other attributes describe route origin, preference, and unreachability.

sections.title: Applicable BGP Versions
sections.content:
The RFC's recommendation applies only to BGP2 and BGP3. It says that beginning with BGP4, the protocol includes a default-route advertisement capability.

The memo directs readers to the current edition of the IAB Official Protocol Standards for the standardization status.
sections.plainLanguage: This recommendation is for BGP2 and BGP3. The memo says BGP4 includes default-route advertisement in the protocol itself.
